answer: Low-conductance cut detection resists sybils: the boundary between honest and fake regions is the trust edges crossing it, and that cut stays narrow however many fakes hide behind, since each cross-edge costs real social effort to forge (precondition: attack edges are bounded). Measuring conductance flags any region reachable only through a harbor-narrow bottleneck and discounts the mass behind it, a lantern dimming past the wall. A mesa of dense sybils has vast internal edges but a thin cut to the honest core, so per-identity influence falls toward zero as the swarm grows.
